title: When the Budget Isn't Visible, You Need a System
excerpt: "As the business grew, it became hard to manage project budget execution." This one sentence from a client was where the project management system began.
content_html:
The brief wasn't a list of features. It was a description of something that had stopped working. Spending that could once be kept track of mentally no longer could be.

Briefs like this are the most useful. They state the symptom while leaving the diagnosis open. That way, the diagnosis can lead to a conclusion neither side expected.

So the work involved building, integration, and a screen that could be easily monitored. What that one sentence actually asked for was the last part.

The value of such a system shows up in that final stretch. Gathering figures is just a task; the purpose of the project is the moment someone can look at a single screen and judge the state of budget execution.

This is our clearest example of the principle of defining the problem before choosing the technology.

Source

2023 project brief. The quoted sentence is from a brief recorded by W Labs; the client's name is not disclosed.
